Zuph
zŭf
n. (an ancestor of Samuel, and the district named after him)
Hebrew Tsuph, meaning honeycomb. The name belongs to a Kohathite forefather of Samuel and to the territory in Ephraim that carried his name, where Saul was searching for lost asses when he met the prophet.

Biblical Definition

The first book of Samuel opens with a genealogy that reaches back to him: “Now there was a certain man of Ramathaimzophim, of mount Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephrathite” (1 Samuel 1:1). The Chronicler places the same man in the Levitical line, which explains how a family in Ephraim's hill country came to serve at the sanctuary: “The son of Zuph, the son of Elkanah, the son of Mahath, the son of Amasai” (1 Chronicles 6:35). The district took his name, and it is where the kingdom of Israel effectively began: “And when they were come to the land of Zuph, Saul said to his servant that was with him, Come, and let us return; lest my father leave caring for the asses, and take thought for us” (1 Samuel 9:5). Saul was about to give up and go home. His servant suggested asking the man of God in the city, and the meeting that followed made him king. The narrator has already told the reader what was happening: “Now the LORD had told Samuel in his ear a day before Saul came, saying” (1 Samuel 9:15).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no entry for Zuph; the Hebrew signifies honeycomb, and the name belongs to an ancestor of Samuel and to a district of Ephraim.

expand to see more

ZUPH, n. An ancestor of Samuel the prophet, and the name of the district in Ephraim called after him.

RAMATHAIM-ZOPHIM, n. The double height of the watchers; the town of Elkanah and the birthplace of Samuel.

ASS, n. A quadruped of the equine genus, used for burden and for riding in eastern countries.

SEER, n. A prophet; a person who foresees future events; one who has visions from God.

ANOINT, v.t. To pour oil upon; to consecrate by unction, as a king or priest.

Modern Corruption

Guidance is sought in impressions and signs, while Scripture shows an ordinary errand governed invisibly by a God who had already spoken to His prophet a day before.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is how 1 Samuel 9 teaches providence. Saul is not on a spiritual quest; he is looking for his father's donkeys, and by the time he reaches the land of Zuph he is ready to abandon the search because his father will be worrying. Every step is ordinary: lost animals, a long walk, a discouraged young man, a servant with a practical suggestion and a quarter shekel of silver. And the narrator interrupts to say that the LORD had told Samuel in his ear a day before Saul came.

That sentence is the doctrine. Nothing in the errand announced itself as guidance; there was no impression, no sign, no inner voice, and Saul had no idea he was walking toward a throne. The Reformed understanding of God's leading rests here rather than on the modern search for personal revelations: God governs the whole chain of ordinary causes, and the believer's duty is obedience in the errand actually in front of him, whether that is a lost animal or a hard week. The wisdom to be sought is in the word already written; the arrangement of events belongs to the One who spoke to Samuel the day before.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Tsuph (H6689), honeycomb; Ramathayim Tsophim (H7436), the double height of the watchers; ozen (H241), the ear; galah ozen, to uncover the ear, to reveal.

expand to see more

Hebrew Tsuph (H6689) — honeycomb; an ancestor of Samuel and a district of Ephraim.

Hebrew Ramathayim Tsophim (H7436) — Ramathaim-zophim, the town of Elkanah.

Hebrew Elqanah (H511) — Elkanah, God has possessed; the father of Samuel.

Hebrew galah ozen (H1540, H241) — to uncover the ear; the LORD told Samuel in his ear.

Hebrew athon (H860) — a she-ass; the animals Saul was seeking.

Usage

"“The son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephrathite” — Samuel's descent."

"“When they were come to the land of Zuph” — where Saul nearly turned back."

"“The LORD had told Samuel in his ear a day before” — the hidden arrangement."
